facts.text: The common bronzewing is a heavily built pigeon native to Australia and one of the country's most common pigeons.
facts.quote: Native to Australia and one of the country's most common pigeons, the common bronzewing is able to live in almost any habitat

facts.text: Its advertising call is an extraordinary mournful whooo repeated at metronomic intervals.
facts.quote: Its advertising call is an extraordinary mournful whooo repeated at metronomic intervals.

facts.text: Male common bronzewings have pale-yellow to yellow-white foreheads and pink breasts.
facts.quote: Males of the species have pale-yellow to yellow-white foreheads, and pink breasts.

facts.text: Both sexes have a clearly visible white line around their eyes.
facts.quote: Both males and females have an easily discernible white line around and proximate to their eyes.

facts.text: Common bronzewings show patches of red, blue and green on their wings.
facts.quote: Common bronzewings also have patches of red, blue and green on their wings

facts.text: It lives in almost any habitat except very barren areas and dense rainforests.
facts.quote: the common bronzewing is able to live in almost any habitat, with the possible exception of very barren areas and dense rainforests.

facts.text: It rarely strays far from water, drinking frequently, and is usually cautious and hard to approach.
facts.quote: Rarely found far from a source of water, common bronzewings either travel alone or in pairs or in flocks, and are usually cautious, making approach by humans or other animals difficult.

facts.text: Its diet is mainly seeds and all varieties of vegetables, and searching for food can last for days.
facts.quote: The common bronzewing's diet primarily consists of seeds and all varieties of vegetables. It searches for food in small groups. The search can sometimes last for days

facts.text: It builds a rough twig nest low in a tree or bush, with eggs hatching after roughly 14 to 16 days.
facts.quote: Common bronzewings construct a rough nest of twigs and sticks, which is placed low down in a tree or bush. The eggs are incubated by both parents and hatch after roughly 14 to 16 days.

facts.text: Like other pigeons, it feeds its young a milky substance from the crop.
facts.quote: In common with other pigeons, common bronzewings release a milky substance from their crop to feed their young.
